item.title: ¿Y qué pasa cuando lo que se democratiza es el fraude documental?
item.description: La digitalización de los procesos y la irrupción de la inteligencia artificial generativa han hecho que falsificar una factura, un parte o un justificante sea hoy más barato y rápido que nunca. Las técnicas utilizadas por los defraudadores son cada vez más accesibles y sofisticadas, y también más difíciles de detectar.

item.title: Del copago al saldo médico: la fórmula que quiere cambiar el seguro de salud
item.description: Frente a la tradicional elección entre pagar una coste más alto o asumir un gasto cada vez que se utiliza la póliza, empiezan a surgir modelos que plantean una tercera vía: asignar al asegurado un saldo anual para utilizarlo en consultas, pruebas y tratamientos. Conozcamos más sobre este interesante tema que tanta curiosidad suscita.

item.title: Comienza a operar Aqua Insurance, una MGA independiente que aporta soluciones en Transporte y Logística
item.description: Según puede adelantar esta Redacción, los brókeres del mercado español tienen desde hace unas fechas una nueva posibilidad de respuesta a sus problemas de aseguramiento en Transporte y Logística: la agencia de suscripción (MGA) Aqua Insurance. En sus primeros pasos se apoya en dos productos: Responsabilidad Civil de Operador Logístico y Mercancías.

item.title: Judge Says Smucker’s Suit Against Trader Joe’s Over Frozen PB&J Can Proceed
item.description: Smucker can proceed with a lawsuit against Trader Joe’s over frozen sandwiches that Smucker claims are too similar to its Uncrustables. Smucker sued Trader Joe’s in federal court in Ohio last fall, claiming Trader Joe’s committed a trademark violation when it introduced frozen peanut butter and jelly sandwiches with the same round shape and crimped edges as Uncrustables. District Judge John Adams ruled Friday that Smucker had devoted significant resources to developing Uncrustables and protecting the brand over the past 20 years.

item.title: Deutsche Bank And Former Banker Settle $176M Lawsuit for Undisclosed Sum
item.description: Deutsche Bank said it has settled a lawsuit with a second former employee who sought damages in a case involving business with Italy’s Monte dei Paschi, days ahead of a trial that threatened to embroil the bank’s CEO. It was the second settlement in the dispute, leaving the cases of the four other former Deutsche Bank staff who are claiming more than 600 million pounds ($812.16 million) in a London court. The bank has now settled with two of the six former employees who filed the suits.

item.title: The Causation Gap: Why Workers’ Comp Files Stall and What Changes It
item.description: View Series A workers’ comp story claims professionals know all too well — and what’s finally changing it. With caseloads in workers’ comp commonly running between 110 and 140 open files per examiner , and research suggesting that anything over 125 can increase the cost of a claim by up to 20% , the math simply doesn’t work. Fragmented across dozens of documents , duplicated across providers, and contradicted between a treating physician’s note from month two and an IME report from month eight, manual review of a complex workers’ comp file takes days.

item.title: Willis Re hires Neil Eckert as CEO
item.description: Willis Re, the reinsurance advisory and brokerage firm, has appointed reinsurance and capital markets veteran Neil Eckert as its new Chief Executive Officer (CEO). Eckert joins Willis Re from Bermuda-based reinsurer Conduit Re, which he co-founded in 2020. Eckert will take up his position at Willis Re after completing his existing contractual commitments.

item.title: Discipline matters more than growth, right-sizing ILS capital is key: Parry, RenaissanceRe
item.description: In this insurance-linked securities market environment where engagement from investors remains strong, Chris Parry, the Global Head of RenaissanceRe Capital Partners told us that a disciplined approach matters more than growth and right-sizing capital is key at this stage of the reinsurance cycle. Parry feels that ensuring capital is right-sized to the opportunity is critical in disciplined ILS management and this is a key feature of ILS manager discipline at this time. “In our view, protecting underwriting margins and delivering strong returns for our investors over the long-term is far more important than growing assets under management,” Parry explained.

item.title: US P&C underwriting gains improved in H1’26, but performance varied by line of business and geography: Verisk
item.description: US property and casualty (P&C) insurers have posted strong underwriting gains of $31.7 billion through the first half of 2026, up from the $11.6 billion recorded through midyear 2025, according to Verisk and the American Property Casualty Insurance Association (APCIA) data, yet line-specific and geographic challenges persist. Saurabh Khemka, president of Verisk Underwriting Solutions, stated: “First-half results should not be mistaken as evidence that underlying risk has diminished. Broader industry performance highlights the growing value of precision as property market conditions continue to soften.

item.title: Reinsurance industry normalising after exceptionally strong period: BCG
item.description: Boston Consulting Group (BCG) analysts have said the reinsurance industry is normalising after an “exceptionally strong period” of improving pricing, robust returns, and rapid balance-sheet growth, in its new 2026 Insurance Value Creators Report. The report also affirmed that reinsurance remains a strong long-term value creator, generating an average annual TSR of 13.4% over the ten years from 2016 through 2025. Over the five years through 2025, reinsurance generated average annual total shareholder returns (TSR) of 19.1%, but one-year TSR fell sharply from 29% in 2024 to 14% in 2025, albeit still above the 10-year average.

item.title: Eloise Hurley Wellington named Head of Howden Re European Programmes
item.description: Reinsurance broker Howden Re has announced the appointment of Eloise Hurley Wellington to lead Howden Re Programmes Europe. I congratulate Eloise on her appointment and look forward to working with her and the Programmes team to innovate and deliver for our European MGA clients.” Hurley Wellington added, “MGAs are increasingly central to insurance distribution and product development across Europe. Before joining Howden Re, Hurley Wellington held various senior leadership roles at Zurich, most recently serving as Head of MGA, Zurich Global Ventures.

item.title: Intense Los Angeles Heat to Send State’s Power Demand Soaring
item.description: Heat advisories will cover much of California’s coast and Central Valley, including the Bay Area and Los Angeles, through Wednesday and Thursday, the National Weather Service said. Wholesale on-peak power prices in Southern California’s SP15 hub, which includes the Los Angeles metropolitan area, rose as high as $87.69 a megawatt-hour for 6 p.m. Most power being used today was contracted the prior day in the day-ahead market based on demand forecasts.

item.title: Amazon Accused in Lawsuit of Systematic Discrimination Against Pregnant Employees
item.description: The lawsuit seeks lost pay and benefits, punitive damages, and an injunction against discrimination against pregnant employees. 8 in a proposed nationwide class action accusing the retailer of systematically discriminating against thousands of pregnant employees, including by firing some it claimed took too much time off. According to a complaint filed by four former warehouse employees, Amazon routinely violates federal and New York worker-protection laws by denying pregnant workers basic accommodations such as chairs, bathroom and water breaks, and time off for prenatal appointments.

item.title: Trump Administration Stalled a Survey of PFAS in Wastewater, Former EPA Officials Say
item.description: The Trump administration has stalled a study that would help regulators understand which industries dump harmful forever chemicals with their wastewater, according to two former agency officials who were involved in its development. A public notice shows the first of its kind survey of wastewater treatment plants was submitted to the White House for approval nearly two years ago during the Biden administration — a far longer wait than is typical. The Trump administration’s nuanced — and at times controversial — stance towards PFAS The Trump administration has promised to combat PFAS.

item.title: Celerity Risk launches personal brand coverage
item.description: Celerity Risk , part of Ryan Specialty Underwriting Managers, has introduced an endorsement covering financial losses tied to personal brands and social media accounts. The First Party Brand Reputation & Social Media Interruption Enhancement expands Celerity Risk’s media liability offering for creators, athletes, entertainers and other public figures. The coverage is available through Celerity Risk’s media liability platform, subject to underwriting guidelines, limits and individual risk assessment.

item.title: USAA and Bank of America enter patent agreement
item.description: USAA and Bank of America have entered into a patent cross-license agreement allowing each company to use the other’s patent portfolio. This agreement supports the application of innovations from Bank of America and USAA in ways that benefit our clients and contribute to continued progress across the financial services industry.” – David Marx, Business Management and Controls Executive at Bank of America. We look forward to working with other banks and credit unions to create mutually beneficial licensing agreements, just as we have done with Bank of America.” – Mike Chaparro, Investments Principal at USAA.

item.title: Nationwide adds actively managed fund strategy to fixed indexed annuity
item.description: Nationwide claims New Heights Select is the first fixed indexed annuity to include a strategy linked to an actively managed mutual fund. Nationwide , Annexus and Capital Group are adding a strategy linked to the American Funds Growth Fund of America Class F-3 mutual fund to the Nationwide New Heights Select fixed indexed annuity suite. Nationwide and Annexus previously introduced a registered index-linked annuity offering strategies tied to an actively managed fund.

item.title: Orange Goes Live on Solstice Equinox
item.description: (Image source: IIR.) Orange Insurance Exchange (Tampa, Fla.), a Florida-domiciled reciprocal insurance exchange focused on property insurance, has gone live on Solstice Innovations’ Equinox policy administration platform, launching three personal-lines products simultaneously for new business across its Florida portfolio. Orange launched HO-3 homeowners, HO-6 condo and DP-3 dwelling fire products on the Equinox platform Sept. The simultaneous launch of three products reflects Orange’s use of Equinox as a single system for rating, issuance, endorsements, renewals, claims, billing and forms, according to the statement.

item.title: Farmers Prepares Customers for Costlier, Longer Repairs Due to High Tech Cars
item.description: High tech cars of today will likely take longer and be more expensive to repair, according to a recently released customer education campaign by Farmers Insurance. Repair costs can rise for many reasons, and advanced safety technology is just one factor that can make certain repairs more complex, Farmers said. When a car with ADAS is damaged, repairs may require special parts, computer checks and careful adjustments to keep safety features working properly, the California-based insurer said.

item.title: Mistral AI Raises $3.5B At $24B Valuation In Another Record European AI Round
item.description: At the time of Mistral’s $2 billion Series C, that raise represented the largest venture round ever raised by a European AI company. Paris-based generative AI startup Mistral AI said Tuesday that it has nearly doubled its valuation to more than $24 billion with a $3.5 billion Series D fundraise. Samsung Electronics led the round, with participation from co-leads Scaleup Europe Fund, managed by EQT , and existing investor PSG Equity .

item.title: As connected risks collide, industry can build conviction and confidence for capital: Fauber, Moody’s CEO
item.description: As the insurance and reinsurance industry work to understand emerging risks, there’s a need to build the conviction and confidence of all stakeholders including capital providers, so risks can be effectively transferred, according to Moody’s CEO Rob Fauber. He hosted a panel discussion with industry leaders, where the size of the capital pools waiting on the sidelines of reinsurance was highlighted once again and Fauber explained that the industry needs to help capital understand the opportunity and put understanding around it, to give providers the ability to come into the sector with confidence. Fauber was speaking in Monte Carlo this week at a Moody’s hosted briefing focused on the emerging risks being faced by the global economy and society during the 2026 Rendez-vous event.

item.title: When it comes to AI adoption most re/insurers are leaving value on the table: Accenture
item.description: While most insurers are using artificial intelligence (AI) to improve today’s performance, many are “leaving value on the table,” according to Accenture’s new report, ‘How Insurers Drive Revenue by Deploying AI with Intent.’ Accenture surveyed 263 senior insurance executives with direct accountability for AI, data, technology, and business transformation across the Americas, Europe, and Asia-Pacific. 83% of respondents reported moderate-to-severe gaps in linking AI capabilities to measurable outcomes, and only 32% of leaders are prioritising revenue growth as their main goal, “leaving significant value on the table.” The report also found that 68% of respondents expect AI agents to transform core workflows. The report revealed that more than four in five (81%) insurers are seeing real revenue gains from AI, achieving at least a 5% improvement in gross written premiums from AI and data initiatives, driven by better pricing, personalisation and cross-selling.

item.title: People Moves: Church Mutual Names Parisi as VP – Head of Finance and FP&A
item.description: Church Mutual Insurance Company has named Ben Parisi vice president, head of finance operations and financial planning and analysis. The newly created role supports the continued evolution of Church Mutual’s finance functions and strengthens its ability to provide the financial insight and operational support the business needs to make informed decisions. Parisi will lead finance operations, expense management, procurement, payroll, financial planning and analysis, and management reporting.

item.title: TrueNorth Launches Property Program for Aging Community Associations and Apartments
item.description: TrueNorth Companies announced a new property program designed to help community associations and apartments owners, including affordable housing and student housing properties, secure broad coverage at a competitive price. TrueNorth built the program around an internal underwriting facility, allowing the firm to evaluate each property on its own merits rather than applying blanket restrictions based on a building’s age or claims history. The program is built to serve community associations — condominiums, homeowners associations and townhome communities — as well as apartment properties across the market-rate and affordable housing and student housing spectrum.

item.title: Insured Loss Estimates Top $600M From Washington Fires, Testing New Commissioner
item.description: The wildfires that plagued Washington for nearly half the summer put new Insurance Commissioner Patty Kuderer and her office to a test. However, she’s relatively new considering her predecessor, Washington Commissioner of Insurance Mike Kreidler, was the nation’s longest serving commissioner, having held the office since 2001. The magnitude of what she and the Office of The Insurance Commissioner are dealing with is best stated in numbers: the blazes resulted in the most expensive fire damage in Washington history, and Spokane County Assessor Tom Konis puts rebuilding costs from three recent wildfires at more than $1 billion.

item.title: Flood Risk Beyond Traditional Zones
item.description: Risk managers must recognize that pluvial flooding now accounts for much of the flood risk in many regions — and that traditional flood maps do not always capture this threat. According to the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), in the United States, the proportions at risk from the three main flood mechanisms are very similar. In continental Europe, France, Germany, and Poland are dominated by fluvial flood risk, but pluvial flooding is the fastest-rising driver.

We've seen plenty of other surprises because the backlash against AI caught Big Tech unawares.

item.title: Zurich expands SME liability offering
item.description: Zurich UK has launched its Combined Liability product on Acturis Open Market and Zurich Online, expanding its SME e-trading offering. Zurich built the offering on its existing SME Commercial Combined infrastructure. The product gives brokers access to more than 1,400 additional trades and allows them to quote and bind liability-only coverage through either platform.

item.title: weSure acquires UBIC
item.description: weSure plans to combine UBIC’s carrier operations with its underwriting technology and Hourly’s payroll capabilities. weSure Digital Insurance Services has acquired Utah Business Insurance Company , expanding its US workers’ compensation operations. Utah-based UBIC provides workers’ compensation coverage across industries including construction, transportation, agriculture, manufacturing, retail, hospitality and healthcare.

item.title: Transamerica names retirement distribution leaders
item.description: Both executives will report to Darren Zino, head of retirement distribution. Transamerica supports more than $253 billion in retirement plan assets and said it is seeing sales growth in pooled plans and increased demand for IRA and stable-value products. Transamerica has appointed Kevin Murphy as national sales manager for the large market and promoted Danny Kling to national sales manager for the mid-market.

item.title: EigenRisk Integrates GeoX Property Data
item.description: “Bringing GeoX’s property data into EigenRisk gives underwriters and reinsurers a much clearer, parcel-level view of what they’re actually insuring,” comments Jacob Grob, EVP of U.S. (Image source: GeoX website.) EigenRisk (Ann Arbor, Mich.) has integrated GeoX (New York) property intelligence into its EigenPrism catastrophe-risk management platform. GeoX’s property intelligence dataset is integrated directly into EigenPrism, where users can augment exposure data with building attributes and analytics for their books of business.

item.title: Hurricane Lowell Brings Heavy Rains as It Passes West of Hawaii
item.description: Hurricane Lowell passed west of Hawaii, where heavy rains may cause hundreds of millions of dollars of damage. Lowell, with top winds of 105 miles (169 kilometers) per hour, edged west of Kauai but is still dropping heavy rain, as well as sending pounding surf across the US state and island chain, the US National Hurricane Center said in an advisory. “Periods of heavy rainfall associated with Lowell will overspread the Hawaiian Islands through Wednesday,” Brad Reinhart, a senior hurricane specialist at the center, wrote in a forecast analysis.

item.title: After $240M Bitcoin Theft, Crypto Scammers’ Spending Spree Comes to an End
item.description: The scammers — a network of young men in their late teens or early 20s — celebrated the August 2024 heist by embarking on a wild spending spree. Cybersecurity researcher Allison Nixon, who has spent years tracking The Com, an underground subculture of young hackers united by the “insane amount of money” that crypto fraud can generate, advocates for more law enforcement resources to go after them. history, duping a stranger out of bitcoin worth over $240 million.

item.title: OpenAI Commits $1B to Cyberdefense Effort Amid AI Safety Scrutiny
item.description: OpenAI has faced increased scrutiny since its own AI agent breached systems at open-source platform Hugging Face during a July test and attempted to hide its actions. OpenAI said on Thursday it would commit $1 billion in subsidized access to its AI cybersecurity tools, training and technical support for organizations that protect critical services, as concerns grow over increasingly sophisticated AI-enabled cyberattacks. OpenAI on Thursday, alongside the cybersecurity initiative, also unveiled Astra, a new AI model it described as its most capable yet but said can at times attempt to evade human monitoring.

item.title: Detroit Sees First Tornado in Nearly 30 Years
item.description: Severe storms last week in Southeastern Michigan led to the first tornado touchdown in 30 years for Detroit, according to a report from the National Weather Service. This was the first confirmed tornado in the city of Detroit since the F2 that impacted the city on July 2, 1997. The line also spawned a brief EF-0 tornado in Lincoln Park and an EF-2 tornado on the east side of Detroit.

item.title: There’s a massive amount of capital looking to enter our industry: Superczynski, Aon
item.description: The insurance and reinsurance industry has an opportunity to harness the appetite of global investors to support growth and help find the capacity to make more risks insurable, because “there is a massive amount of capital that’s looking to enter our industry,” according to Kelly Superczynski, Head of Global Capital Advisory at Aon’s Reinsurance Solutions. There’s plenty of capacity in the market, it’s just a matter of how we get people coming forwards.” Moving on to discuss the potential to grow the insurance and reinsurance industry’s capital base meaningfully, Superczynski said she sees no lack in capital appetite, just that the risks need to be made more accessible to investors. If you look at it in the context of a $250 trillion alternative investment market, our insurance industry is dwarfed by the amount of capital that’s sitting out there in investable capital.

item.title: Peak Re plans to reignite third-party capital business, partner with investors: CUO Hough
item.description: Peak Reinsurance Company (Peak Re), a global reinsurer headquartered in Hong Kong, has plans to “reignite” its third-party capital management business in 2027, seeing itself as having a differentiated offering for investors and wanting to become more sophisticated in the space, Chief Underwriting Officer Philip Hough told Artemis. The company has ambitions and plans underway to become more active again in the third-party capital management space, seeing partnerships with investors as a key way to grow its expanding global reinsurance business. Speaking with us in an interview at the Monte Carlo Rendez-vous event, Hough explained that Peak Re’s third-party capital management unit, Peak Capital, remains licensed in Bermuda and ready to go.

item.title: ILS market structurally healthy, but faces crucial test in cycle management: Steiger, Icosa
item.description: Following several years of strong returns and renewed inflows, the insurance-linked securities (ILS) market currently sits in a structurally healthy position, however this recent momentum must be balanced with disciplined cycle management, Florian Steiger, CEO and Founder of Icosa Investments told Artemis in an interview. Steiger described the current state of the ILS market as “structurally healthy” and increasingly mature, whilst noting that the space continues to normalise following a number of exceptionally attractive years. Speaking to Artemis just before the 2026 Monte Carlo Rendez-Vous de Septembre (RVS) reinsurance industry event, Steiger reflected on the current state of the ILS market, and also shared what Icosa’s views are regarding the rise of AI across the ILS space.

item.title: Vantage appoints Yves Charbonneau as Chief Risk Officer
item.description: (Vantage), a specialty insurance and reinsurance business, has announced the appointment of Yves Charbonneau as Chief Risk Officer. Marc Grandisson, Executive Chairman of Vantage, said, “Yves’s track record, from building enterprise risk frameworks in Bermuda to leading capital and reserving discipline across multiple platforms, reflects the exact rigour we need at the centre of Vantage’s risk function as we continue our momentum under Howard Hughes Holdings.” Charbonneau commented, “Vantage has built a dynamic, highly differentiated platform across the North American and Bermuda re/insurance markets. in Bermuda, including Chief Risk Officer, Chief Actuary, and Head of Actuarial Function for Arch Re Europe.

item.title: EigenRisk expands EigenPrism catastrophe risk management platform with GeoX integration
item.description: EigenRisk, a provider of catastrophe risk management technology, has entered into a new agreement with GeoX, an AI-powered property intelligence company, to expand the EigenPrism catastrophe risk management platform, allowing clients access to granular, AI-derived property attributes across over 186 million US commercial and residential properties. “By pairing EigenRisk’s platform with our imagery analytics across 186 million US properties, we’re making it easy for teams to evaluate portfolio risk in seconds without getting bogged down by manual checks.” Last month, EigenRisk integrated Weatherwatch , an Australian company specialising in storm and weather risk management services, into EigenPrism. EigenRisk continues to expand its data partnership ecosystem with over 40 data providers in its platform, combining catastrophe analytics, hazard intelligence, and property attributes to deliver a more comprehensive view of risk.

item.title: Ceded US health insurance premium sees 300%+ growth over the past decade: AM Best
item.description: Over the past decade, the volume of ceded US health insurance premium to the reinsurance market has grown more than 300%, to USD 203 billion in 2025 from USD 59 billion in 2016, a new AM Best report has revealed. Ceded premium growth has been in double digits in three of the past five years, including 2024 and 2025 when ceded premiums increased by 30% or more. health insurance segments have been under pressure, prompting insurers to seek additional reinsurance support to manage large claims exposure and improve capital efficiency while looking to reduce earnings volatility,” said Jennifer Asamoah, senior financial analyst, AM Best.

item.title: A $320 Million Hack Exposes the Cracks in Crypto’s Plumbing
item.description: The $320 million hack of the Bitcoin-linked Liquid Network is another dent to crypto’s reputation as the industry tries to convince banks and institutional investors that digital assets can become part of mainstream financial infrastructure. The Liquid Network hack this week is the latest in a spate of breaches targeting decentralized platforms this year, including on Kelp DAO and Drift Protocol that together accounted for $588 million in losses. In this instance the hackers returned 3,400 of the Bitcoin, keeping about $47 million worth, according to Alex Thorn, head of research at crypto firm Galaxy Digital Inc.

item.title: AI Could Pose ‘Existential’ Risk to Humanity, UN Rights Chief Warns
item.description: rights chief Volker Turk warned on Monday that artificial intelligence could pose a threat to humanity, and pledged to press AI firms to reduce risks that his office said included disruptions to services, communications and democratic systems. “I share the concerns of industry insiders that advanced AI could pose an existential risk to humanity,” Turk told the body in Geneva. “I am calling here, today, for an all-out effort to put cast-iron guarantees in place around the safety and security of AI, before it is too late.” Turk did not elaborate on the nature of the risks but a spokesperson for his office said failures involving powerful AI systems could disrupt critical infrastructure and democratic institutions.
